newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BRAZILIANS CENTRE-STAGE FOR TOP SPANISH CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZILIANS CENTRE-STAGE FOR TOP SPANISH CLASH.

text.p: A host of Brazilians will be centre-stage when Barcelona travel to Deportivo Coruna in a Spanish league match on Saturday that could prove decisive in both sides' championship bids.

But Deportivo's Renaldo may find his debut alongside Rivaldo and against Barcelona striker Ronaldo marred by conditions that are hardly reminiscent of Rio in January. North-west Spain has been hit by blizzards that threaten to destroy the game as a spectacle.
The threat to the fixture is ironic in view of the battle waged by Deportivo chairman Augusto Lendoiro to ensure the game was played at the club's Riazor ground.

Sports authorities had ruled the stadium should be closed after a coin was thrown from the crowd in a match earlier this season, but reckoned without the pugnatious Lendoiro, who appealed to the civil law courts to have the sentence suspended.
The move was typical of the man who has led Deportivo's bid to break the Real Madrid-Barcelona duopoly of the Spanish game in recent years.
After seeing his side narrowly escape relegation in 1992, Lendoiro signed Bebeto and, with the international striker in the vanguard, Deportivo bounced back to made a strong bid for the title.

The similarities between Portuguese and the Galician language made Deportivo a natural choice for other Brazilians and, with the arrival of Mauro Silva and Donato, Deportivo came desperately close to taking the 1994 championship.
Only a last-minute penalty miss in the final game of the season handed the title to Barcelona.
Deportivo were in the running again the following year, and after a more modest 1995-96 season have signed a string of reinforcements, among them the powerful Brazilian midfielder Rivaldo.
As in previous seasons, third-placed Deportivo's only obvious weakness is up front, a problem exacerbated in the last game before Christmas when French forward Michael Madar was carried off.
Striker Renaldo, a new signing from Atletico Mineiro who has already excited the interest of several Italian and German clubs, is seen as the man to fill the gap.
Not surprisingly Barcelona manager Bobby Robson is full of admiration for his opponents, saying: "Deportivo have got a good team, very strong in midfield."
John Toshack, the Welshman in charge at Deportivo, has returned the compliment to the former England coach.
"They've got the strongest squad in Spain and perhaps in Europe," said Toshack, who confessed he had no special plan to counter brilliant young Barcelona forward Ronaldo.
"(My defenders) are very clever, it's their job not mine," he joked.
One Brazilian Toshack doesn't have to worry about is Barcelona midfielder Giovanni, who will miss the game through injury.
